title: The Napoleonic Wars (1803–1815)
key_facts: Series of global conflicts declared by the French Republic and later French Empire under Napoleon Bonaparte
Coalitions of European powers repeatedly formed against France; wars spanned from Iberia to Russia
Ended with Napoleon’s defeat at Waterloo and the Congress of Vienna (1814–15)
causes: French Revolutionary wars exported revolutionary ideals and military expansion across Europe
Napoleon’s ambition to dominate Europe and restructure continental order
Resistance of established monarchies to French hegemony and revolutionary reforms
outcome: Defeat and abdication of Napoleon; restoration of Bourbon monarchies
Redrawing of European map at the Congress of Vienna
Rise of nationalism, balance-of-power diplomacy, and conservative reaction

figures.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
figures.role: Emperor of the French; architect of the wars

figures.name: Klemens von Metternich
figures.role: Austrian statesman; architect of the Congress of Vienna

impacts: Spread of modern nationalism and concepts of citizen armies
Redefined European borders and state system for a century
Catalyzed the rise of modern conservatism and liberal reforms
